summary: DB-023 authored 20260928010000_event_posts_and_event_claims.sql: the first migration in this repository to create public.event_posts or public.event_claims, both of which live routes read and write. It was proved on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster (154 checks, 0 failures, 13 negative controls each demonstrated failing) and NOTHING WAS APPLIED (CP-051). The apply, the postflight and the real-caller probes are the operator's, and they are the only thing between this file and `staging_validated`. THE PREFLIGHT IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS FILE IS RIGHT FOR YOUR TARGET, SO READ IT BEFORE APPLYING. Both relations may already exist on some environment, created out of band: DB-002 documents prior application by raw Management API SQL, so that is a real possibility and not a hypothetical. `create table if not exists` will SKIP a pre-existing relation and the file's in-transaction post-condition will then ABORT it, naming every differing contract entry. That refusal is the designed outcome, not a failure of the file: it means the target already holds a public.event_posts of unknown shape, which is a decision for a person and not for a no-op. The ONE difference the file does repair on a pre-existing table is `author_id`, because two live writers require it and it is absent from every archived definition. TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE PROBING. (1) The file grants `select on public.event_attendance to authenticated` -- a DEPENDENCY grant on a table it does not create, needed because two of the event_posts policies evaluate a subquery against it. Two live routes (app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts:113 and app/api/events/[id]/page/route.ts:97) ALREADY depend on that grant and the chain never issues it, so this fixes a pre-existing latent break as well. `anon` is deliberately NOT granted it. (2) After the apply, GET /api/events/[id]/posts and GET /api/events/[id]/page will move from 'relation does not exist' to a PostgREST embed error, because both select `profiles:user_id (...)` and the canonical FK shape points at auth.users. That is routed to the events lane (HF-DB023-EVENT-POSTS-CALLERS) and is NOT a reason to withhold the apply: a missing relation is strictly worse than a named embed error, and the fix has a precedent in lib/feed/feed-posts-query.ts:3.
